references.text: The same introductory formula where the Lord speaks to Moses, a common formula in the books of Moses that introduces divine commands.
The opening of Leviticus uses the same formula for the Lord's speech to Moses, establishing the pattern for divine revelation in the book.
An identical introductory formula in the same book, introducing legislation concerning the sin offering.
The same expression is used to introduce further instructions about offerings in Leviticus.
Numbers opens with the same formula for the Lord's speech to Moses, showing continuity in divine communication.
One of many places in Exodus where this formula is used to introduce God's instructions to Moses.
